title: Evaluation of internal Hom on an affine open is bijective
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $\mathcal F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module. For every affine open $U\subset X$, the map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal M,\mathcal F))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal M(U),\mathcal F(U))$ sending a morphism on the opens over $U$ to its component at $U$ is bijective. Internal Hom is the sheaf in [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. No quasi-coherence or finite-presentation hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01I7, lemma-compare-constructions; duality.tex Tag 0BUZ, sections clause

proof.text: Construct the equivalence from internal-Hom sections over U to morphisms on Spec Γ(X,U), using the fully faithful forgetful functor, overEquiv, overFunctorEquiv, restriction along the affine chart isomorphism, and restrictFunctorComp. Construct the Γ(X,U)-linear section equivalences using restrictAppIso and fromSpec image top = U. Their terminal-component compatibility is lem-sc-internal-hom-affine-chart-evaluation. These constructions require no quasi-coherence of the target.

For the quasi-coherent source on the affine chart, precomposition with the invertible tilde/Gamma counit gives a Hom equivalence. Compose with tilde.adjunction.homEquiv. By the right triangle identity this equivalence is precisely the global-sections morphism map. Compose its bijectivity with the chart morphism equivalence, ModuleCat.homEquiv, and the section linear-map equivalence; the terminal-component compatibility identifies this composite with the target evaluation function.
